newsitem.title: INDONESIA: JAKARTA CALL MONEY TRADED AT 17.0 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: JAKARTA CALL MONEY TRADED AT 17.0 PERCENT.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 17.0 percent on Tuesday morning on a slightly tighter market due to weekly tax payments, dealers said.
They said overnight money was at 17.0 percent since the morning, suggesting relatively high tax payments at mid-month.
A balance of 581 billion rupiah was available to the market from maturing central bank papers.
One local bank dealer said longer-term rates were also slightly up due to firming short-term rates. One-week money was at 17.0 percent and one-month money at 16.5 percent.
The central bank kept its rates of bilateral central bank certificates (SBIs) unchanged and continued to be absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market.

Bank Indonesia kept overnight SBIs at 14.0 percent, two-to-six day at 15.0 percent, one-week at 9.5 percent, two-week at 10.0, one-month at 10.625, three at 10.5, six at 11.125 and one-year at 11.75 percent.
Dealers said artificially high central bank short-term rates were likely to continue as the foreign exchange market remained volatile on regional uncertainties.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 15.62 percent, compared with 16.52 percent on Friday.
